title: Families with Anorexia nervosa: Stress experienced by parents of adolescents with anorexia nervosa
summary: Anorexia nervosa is a serious mental illness that places a heavy burden on affected adolescents and their families. The FAN-Stress study examines the extent to which mothers and fathers of young patients with anorexia are affected—both in everyday life and on a physical level. Therefore, parents fill out questionnaires that ask about issues such as the burden caused by anorexia and their own experiences of stress. In addition, a hair sample is used to measure the level of the stress hormone cortisol in the body. Parents are also asked what kind of support they would like to receive in this difficult situation. The measures are conducted at three time points: at the start of treatment in a child and adolescent psychiatric clinic, upon discharge, and two months later. To ensure that the results can be properly classified, a group of parents of healthy adolescents is surveyed for comparison purposes – but only once.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Mothers and fathers of female adolescents aged between 12 and 17.
AN group: Daughter in (partial) inpatient child and adolescent psychiatric treatment due to a diagnosis of anorexia nervosa (according to ICD-10: F50.0 or F50.1).
GES group: Daughter physically and mentally healthy.
Exclusion criteria:
Parents' insufficient knowledge of German, which makes it impossible for them to answer the questionnaires.
